permit_guide.1. Residential Building Permit (RBP): Required for new decks attached to a dwelling at any height; for free-standing decks more than 30 inches above grade at any point; for additions, porches with roofs, and structural alterations. Submittal: site plan, framing plan showing joist size and spacing, footing detail, ledger attachment detail (attached decks only), and contractor license number or owner-builder affidavit.
permit_guide.2. Minor Alteration Permit (MA): Non-structural interior work such as replacing cabinets, drywall under 200 sq ft, and like-for-like window replacement without enlarging openings. Not available for decks, porches or any exterior structure.
permit_guide.3. Exempt work: Free-standing decks not more than 30 inches above grade at any point, not serving a required exit door, and under 200 sq ft. Exempt work must still meet zoning setbacks. Replacement of an existing deck is treated the same as a new deck.
permit_guide.4. Zoning Clearance (ZC): Required in addition to any building permit when the structure is within 5 ft of a property line or in a historic overlay district.
permit_guide.5. Fees: Plan review fee is due at submittal; permit fee is due at issuance. RBP deck plan review: $185. Deck permit fee: $2.10 per sq ft. MA: flat $95.
permit_guide.6. Inspections: Footing, framing and final inspections are required for every RBP deck. Ledger flashing is checked at framing.
permit_guide.7. Guards: Guards are required where the walking surface is more than 30 inches above grade.

program.title: Senior Homestead Assessment Freeze - Ordinance 9-12
program.§1 Eligibility: The owner must (a) be 65 or older on January 1 of the application year, (b) occupy the property as their principal residence, and (c) have household income at or below the limit certified by the Treasurer.
program.§2 Surviving spouse: A surviving spouse of a person who received the freeze may continue the freeze on the same property if the surviving spouse is at least 60 and continues to occupy it as a principal residence. The surviving spouse need not re-establish the income condition in the year of the spouse's death, but must meet (c) in later years.
program.§3 Principal residence: An owner may claim only one principal residence. A homestead exemption active on another parcel is disqualifying until it is released.
program.§4 Filing: Applications must be filed by the date printed on the annual notice; late applications are processed for the following year.
program.§5 Recapture: If the property is sold or stops being the principal residence, the freeze ends.
program.§6 Appeals: Denials may be appealed to the Board of Review within the period printed on the denial notice.

program_manual.CCAP 7.2 Reporting changes: Families must report a new address, a change in household members or a new job to their worker. Reports may be made by phone, portal or in person.
program_manual.CCAP 8.1 Fair hearings: An applicant may request a fair hearing on any denial, reduction or delay in processing.

records_policy.BWC-1: Body-worn camera recordings are public records subject to the exemptions below.
records_policy.BWC-2 Active investigation: A recording may be withheld while it relates to an open criminal investigation or prosecution, if release would reasonably be expected to interfere with it. Once the matter is closed with no charges, or adjudicated, this exemption no longer applies.
records_policy.BWC-3 Subject access: A person who is the subject of a recording, or their attorney, may obtain an unredacted copy of the portions depicting them, except where BWC-2 applies.
records_policy.BWC-4 Privacy redactions: Faces and identifying details of bystanders, minors, victims and witnesses, and of any other person who is not the requesting subject, must be redacted before release. Portions showing the interior of a private residence are redacted unless the resident consents.
records_policy.BWC-5 Third-party consent: A person depicted may waive redaction of themselves only by written, signed consent.
records_policy.BWC-6 Format and fees: Recordings are provided as MP4 on physical media at a $10 media fee or by secure download at no charge. Redaction time is billed at the clerk hourly rate after the first hour.
records_policy.BWC-7 Retention: Non-evidentiary recordings are retained 190 days; recordings tagged to an incident are retained until the case closes plus 3 years.

statute_excerpt.§12-81(20)(b): The exemption continues for the unremarried surviving spouse of a qualifying veteran. It ends if the surviving spouse remarries. If that later marriage ends by divorce or death, eligibility is restored upon new application.

statute_excerpt.§12-81(20)(d): Only one exemption under this section per property.

statute_excerpt.§12-81(20)(f): Applications are filed with the assessor of the town where the property is located. Late filing results in the exemption beginning with the following assessment year.

era_rules.ERA 1 Eligibility: Renter households with income at or below 50% of area median income (system field income_band) that have experienced a financial hardship during the current lease year.
era_rules.ERA 2 Documentation: Hardship may be documented by a termination letter, a reduced-hours statement from the employer, medical bills, or a signed self-attestation when documents are unavailable.
era_rules.ERA 3 Priority: Households with a court-filed eviction or a written notice to vacate are processed first.
era_rules.ERA 4 Exclusions: Assistance may not be paid for any month already covered by ERA. Households living in public housing are excluded. Housing Choice Voucher holders are eligible only for the tenant's share of rent.
era_rules.ERA 5 Landlord participation: Payments go to the landlord, who must sign the landlord agreement. If the landlord refuses to sign or does not respond after two contact attempts, payment may be made to the tenant.
era_rules.ERA 6 Maximum: Up to 12 months of assistance per household across all ERA applications, including arrears and future rent.
era_rules.ERA 7 Utilities: Utility arrears may be included only when the tenant pays the utility directly and provides a current bill.
era_rules.ERA 8 Program integrity: Staff must refer suspected false statements to the Program Integrity Unit and must not deny on suspicion alone.

state.protection_rule: Tariff Rule 22.6 (Elderly and Minor Households). The utility shall not disconnect residential service for nonpayment where every adult resident of the premises is 65 or older, or where the only other residents are under 18. This protection does not apply if the utility has offered a deferred payment arrangement in writing and the customer has declined it in writing or failed to respond to two written offers. records_rules.R-12 Rolling release: Large requests may be released in installments as review is completed.

state.call_transcript: Caller: Our power's been out since yesterday morning. I got a portable generator going, it's in the garage with the big door open, and I plugged it into the dryer outlet with one of those double-plug cords my brother-in-law made so the whole house has power. I think I flipped the main breaker off first but honestly I'm not sure, it was dark. When are you guys getting to Hollis Court?
state.agent_checklist: Ask: Is the generator connected to house wiring? Is there a transfer switch or interlock? Is the main breaker off? Where is the generator located?

safety_guide.SG-1 Backfeed: A generator connected to house wiring without a transfer switch or interlock can energize the utility's lines and electrocute line workers. If a caller reports this, flag the premise 'BACKFEED RISK' for crews and tell the caller to unplug the generator from house wiring immediately.
safety_guide.SG-2 Main breaker: If the caller cannot confirm the main breaker is off, treat the connection as an active backfeed hazard.
safety_guide.SG-3 Carbon monoxide: Generators must run outdoors, at least 20 ft from doors and windows. Running one in a garage, even with the door open, is a CO poisoning risk; advise moving it outside.

R-1: Eligible applicants are (a) aged 60 or older by the end of the season, or (b) aged 55-59 with a disability and living in a senior housing facility that participates in the program. Dear Rent Calculation Unit,

I received my annual recertification letter dated April 10 saying my share of rent is going from $286 to $412 starting June 1. I have a few things to say.

First, I think the new amount is wrong. The letter says you counted $480 a month from 'unearned income - contributions'. That is money my brother sends sometimes to help with my medicine, it is not every month and it is not income, it is for my prescriptions. Some months he sends nothing. Second, as you know I use a wheelchair since my stroke. The recertification interview was held on the third floor of your office and the elevator was out of service. I had to do the interview on the phone in the lobby with no privacy, with other people sitting right there listening to my income and my medical information. I would like my future appointments to be at a location I can get to, or by home visit.

Third, I also have medical expenses (prescriptions, the wheelchair repair) that I did not know I could report. I am attaching receipts from the last 12 months. I understand these can be deducted for disabled households. My neighbor in 4B told me she gets a deduction like this every year.

I have lived at Harbor Terrace for nine years and always reported everything. I don't understand why this year is different. My caseworker, Ms. Albright, retired in January and I have not been assigned a new one; nobody answers the number on the letter. The letter also says the rent will be recalculated if I report changes, but I never got the worksheet showing how you did the calculation. Could you send it? My sister Mariam helps me read these letters and can call you if you give me a name.

If you cannot fix this, please tell me how to ask for a hearing.

Thank you,
Yusuf Haddad
555-0158

state.tenant_protection_rule: TP-1. When the account for a master-metered residential building (one meter serving several dwelling units, billed to the landlord) is scheduled for disconnection for nonpayment, the utility must post notice in each unit's common entrance and mail notice to 'Occupant' at each unit at least 10 days before disconnection. The winter moratorium does not apply to commercial accounts; master-metered residential buildings billed under a commercial rate are treated as residential for TP-1 and TP-2. TP-4. Before posting, the utility must attempt to reach the landlord by phone and by mail.

INTERNAL AUDIT REPORT IA-26-08: Machining and Assembly, Building 2. Audit dates: 2026-08-25 and 26. Lead auditor: F. Adeyemi (Quality Systems; normally assigned to Building 1 audits). Scope: production control, nonconforming product, monitoring and measuring resources, release of product. Criteria: ISO 9001:2015 plus customer-specific requirements. Records sampled: 30 setup sheets, 40 MRB bins, 22 gauges from the recall list, 12 shipment release packs.

Summary: The area has a mature 5S program and good visual management. Four findings and two opportunities for improvement are recorded. Grading per QP-9.2: MAJOR = absence or total breakdown of a required process, or a situation likely to result in shipment of nonconforming product; MINOR = a single lapse or partial failure that does not by itself put product conformity at risk; OFI = no requirement breached.

Finding 1: Operator sign-off on setup verification sheets was missing for 4 of 30 sampled setups on the HMC cell. This repeats finding IA-25-21 from last year; the corrective action (sheet redesign) was implemented but has not been effective.

Finding 2: In the MRB cage, 3 of 40 bins of nonconforming parts had no red NCR tag. All 3 bins were inside the locked cage and listed on the MRB log, so they were segregated and identified in the system.

Finding 3: A 20 to 100 Nm click torque wrench (asset TW-118) used on assembly station A-4 for final bolt torque had no calibration label and was not in the calibration recall database. Operators said it was brought over from Building 1 two months ago.

Finding 4: Final inspection sign-off was not performed on the weekend shift for the past five weekends because the weekend inspector position is vacant. Product built on those weekends was shipped on Monday mornings on the production supervisor's release.

OFI 1: Consider digital torque data capture on A-4. OFI 2: Floor markings in the receiving area are worn.

Positive observations: Excellent housekeeping in the grinding area; the new first-article checklist is well used and understood by operators.

Area manager comment appended after the closing meeting: Finding 4 should be graded OFI. The supervisor's Monday release counts as final inspection, so the automated grading tool should record it that way.

Next steps: Area owner to submit corrective action plans for findings 1 to 4 by 2026-09-12. Auditee management present at the closing meeting: A. Brennan (Operations Manager), K. Osei (Quality Supervisor).

scar.issue: Short shots (incomplete fill at latch tip) found on 42 of 3,000 pieces at our incoming inspection, lot HP-2231. Two pieces reached our assembly line and failed the latch pull test.

supplier_response.D1: Cross-functional team: process engineer, tooling lead, quality engineer, production supervisor, maintenance planner.
supplier_response.D2: Latch tip short shot on CN-12, cavity 3 and 4 only, tool T-12, all shifts.
supplier_response.D3: Sorted 100% of supplier stock (18,400 pcs), in-transit lot HP-2233 intercepted at the carrier hub and sorted, and a sort team sent to the customer site for lots HP-2229 to HP-2232. 57 rejects total.
supplier_response.D4_occurrence: Hot-runner zone 3 thermocouple on tool T-12 drifted low; controller showed setpoint while the actual nozzle temperature was below the processing window. Confirmed by an independent thermocouple and by reproducing short shots in a trial with zone 3 deliberately lowered.
supplier_response.D4_escape: The vision system recipe checked only pin presence, not latch-tip fill, so short latches passed.
supplier_response.D5: Replaced the zone 3 thermocouple; added a redundant thermocouple with a deviation alarm that interlocks the press (stops injection) when the two readings disagree; vision recipe updated to inspect latch-tip fill at 4 locations with a challenge part at each shift start.
supplier_response.D6: Since implementation: 26 production days, 212,000 pieces, zero short shots at vision or at customer incoming inspection. Interlock challenge-tested weekly.
supplier_response.D7: Redundant thermocouple and interlock deployed to all 14 hot-runner tools in the plant; PFMEA and control plan updated for the CN family; thermocouple replacement added to the PM schedule.

state.incoming_inspection_since_fix: Lots HP-2240 to HP-2251 received and inspected at normal sampling: zero short shots.

8D TEAM MEETING MINUTES, CAPA-26-131, brazed-joint leaks on evaporator coil EC-600. Date: 2026-09-09. Attendees: P. Nwachukwu (QE, facilitator), L. Soto (production supervisor), G. Ferreira (brazing lead), M. Chu (incoming inspection), R. Ivanova (plant manager, joined late).

Problem statement: Since mid-August, final leak-test rejects on EC-600 rose from the usual one or two per week to between five and nine per week. All leaks are at return-bend joints brazed at station B3.

Fishbone brainstorm (ideas only, not verified at the time):
- Man: new brazer (J. Park, started 08/04) may be overheating joints.
- Machine: torch tip wear on B3; the gas flow meter reads erratically.
- Method: flux paste application changed from brush to syringe in July.
- Material: copper tube lot T-7781 (first used 08/12) may carry drawing-oil residue.
- Measurement: leak tester sensitivity was raised after the July calibration.
- Environment: the dock door near B3 is often left open, and drafts may cool the joints.

Verification actions and results (week 37):
1. Joints by brazer: the leak rate per brazer over two weeks is essentially the same for all four brazers, including J. Park.
2. Torch tip replaced 09/02; leaks continued at the same rate afterwards.
3. Flux: the syringe method has been used since July, but the leak rise began mid-August; July output was normal.
4. Tube cleanliness: residue test on five samples from lot T-7781 found oil residue above the cleanliness specification on three samples; five samples from the earlier lot T-7702 were all clean.
5. Reproduction: 20 joints brazed from T-7781 tube produced 4 leakers; 20 joints from T-7702 produced none, same brazer, same torch, same day.
6. Dock door: leak rejects occurred on days the door log shows closed as well as open.
7. Leak tester: no action taken yet.

Conclusion: Verified occurrence root cause is drawing-oil residue on tube lot T-7781 preventing braze wetting. Escape point: incoming inspection checks tube dimensions and certificates only; no cleanliness test is done at receiving.

Plant manager comment (recorded at her request): 'I still think it's the new guy, he has been rushing the joints.'

Attachment A (leak data summary): Rejects by week for weeks 31 to 37 are attached as a chart; the rise starts in week 33, the first full week after lot T-7781 went into use. Rejects by coil position show all leaks on return bends, none on header joints, which are brazed at station B1 with tube from the same supplier but a different lot.

Actions: quarantine remaining T-7781 stock (M. Chu); SCAR to the tube supplier (P. Nwachukwu); add a cleanliness wipe test at receiving (M. Chu); review leak tester settings (owner to be decided).

ncr.initial_description: Linear crack about 35 mm long on the outer wall near the inlet flange, visible after rough machining. Dye penetrant shows a continuous line indication. 4 of 120 castings from lot GF-4410.
ncr.containment: Lot GF-4410 held. The 38 machined housings in WIP were dye-penetrant inspected: only the 4 already found show indications.

lab_report.sections: Two castings sectioned across the indication.

cdd_policy_trusts.§5.1: For express trusts, identify and verify: the settlor; each trustee (for a corporate trustee, the entity plus the directors who act for it); any protector; each named beneficiary; and any other natural person exercising ultimate effective control over the trust.
cdd_policy_trusts.§5.2: Where beneficiaries are designated by class (for example 'descendants of the settlor'), record a description of the class sufficient to identify a beneficiary when a distribution is made; individual verification is required at the time of the first distribution to that person.
cdd_policy_trusts.§5.3: EDD is required where a trustee is resident or incorporated in a jurisdiction on the bank's high-risk list, or where the trust holds interests in operating companies in such a jurisdiction.
cdd_policy_trusts.§5.4: The source of the trust assets (the settlor's source of wealth) must be recorded; if the settlor is deceased, the file must document the origin of the settled assets from probate or equivalent records.

state: BLOCKCHAIN ANALYTICS ALERT BA-2026-771, customer CUS-80442 (Ms. Rana Idris, graphic designer), crypto-brokerage account.
Tool finding 1: In August the customer withdrew the equivalent of about USD 38,000 in bitcoin to an external address. The tool attributes that address, with 'high confidence', to a mixing service.
Tool finding 2: Two weeks later, the customer deposited the equivalent of about USD 36,000 in bitcoin from a different external address with no attribution.

Customer response to the information request: 'I use a privacy wallet because I was hacked last year. I moved my own coins out and back.' She provided a screenshot of a wallet app showing the two transactions under her profile name.

Firm policy CX-9 §2: Transactions with mixing services are high risk; obtain an explanation and evidence of ownership of the addresses involved. §3: Where ownership of the returning funds cannot be evidenced, escalate to investigations. §4: A wallet screenshot alone is not evidence of address ownership; a signed message from the address is accepted.
Profile: expected activity 'occasional crypto purchases for investment, a few thousand USD per year'.

Account history: the customer bought bitcoin in small amounts from her salary between 2023 and early 2026; the total bought over that time is close to the amount later withdrawn in August. No earlier withdrawals to external addresses.
Hack claim: the customer's file contains a 2025 support ticket in which she reported a phishing email and asked for her password to be reset; no loss of funds was recorded at our platform.

Analyst note: the returning address received its funds in several pieces from different sources shortly before sending to us; the tool cannot link them to the mixer output, and it cannot link them to any illicit source either.

Follow-up request: on 09/10 the analyst asked the customer to sign a message from the returning address, as §4 allows. The customer replied that she 'did not know how' and asked whether a video of her wallet app would do instead. No signed message has been received.

Market note: the bitcoin price moved only slightly between the withdrawal and the return, so the difference between the amounts withdrawn and returned is mostly accounted for by the mixer's fee, according to the analyst's rough estimate.
Peer comparison: of the platform's customers who used mixing services in 2026, most were later found to be privacy-minded users with legitimate funds; a minority were linked to scams or stolen funds.

state: INVESTIGATION WORKING NOTES, INV-2026-0455. Subjects: four customer companies, all with accounts at our bank: Arden Metals Ltd (CUS-5101), Brisk Freight Ltd (CUS-5102), Calder Services Ltd (CUS-5103), Dunmore Trading Ltd (CUS-5104).
Link analysis: all four companies share the same accountant and the same registered address; three share a director, M. Farrell; the fourth's director is Farrell's spouse.

Flow summary, June to August 2026: Arden received about EUR 2.2 million from an overseas customer, 'Solace Import FZE'. Within 48 hours Arden paid Brisk EUR 2.1 million for 'transport'. Brisk paid Calder EUR 2.0 million for 'management services'. Calder paid Dunmore EUR 1.9 million for 'materials'. Dunmore paid EUR 1.8 million back to Solace Import FZE as a 'refund of overpayment'.
Invoices: each payment is supported by a one-page invoice with a generic description and no delivery details. Invoice numbers are sequential across different companies.
Profiles: Arden declared expected turnover of EUR 500,000 per year; Brisk EUR 300,000; Calder and Dunmore were dormant until May 2026.
Solace Import FZE: no website; registered in a free zone; the same entity was named in a 2025 public court judgement abroad as a vehicle in a fraud scheme (as a company, not naming individuals).
Other activity: Arden also pays rent and three salaries; the other three companies have no staff costs.

Accountant check: the shared accountant, Pell & Co, is registered with the national accountancy body; a disciplinary notice from 2024 records a reprimand for 'failing to keep adequate client identification records', without further details.
Farrell background: M. Farrell has been a director of several small companies since 2018, most dissolved within two years; no adverse media found on him or his spouse.

Customer contact: Arden's finance manager, asked by the relationship manager about the Solace payments, said Solace 'overpaid by mistake and asked for the balance back through our group'. No correspondence from Solace about an overpayment was supplied.

Retained amounts: after the chain, about EUR 400,000 in total stayed across the four companies (each kept a slice at its step); most of it was later withdrawn in cash or paid to Farrell's personal account as 'director's loan repayment'.

Earlier pattern: a smaller version of the same chain, with a different overseas payer, ran through Arden, Brisk and Calder in February 2026; it was not alerted at the time because each single payment was within Arden's declared profile.
Analyst question list for the team call: typology, strength of layering evidence, whether the funds return to the original sender, next steps.

alert.subject: Employee E-40219, Paula Serrano, branch customer-service officer

findings: Between May and August, seven elderly customers' accounts had their contact phone numbers changed by Ms Serrano's user ID, each followed within days by online-banking activation from a new device.

After activation, each account sent transfers of EUR 2,000 to 6,000 to one of three personal accounts at other banks; two of these accounts are in the names of relatives of Ms Serrano, according to HR next-of-kin records.
In three cases, the branch's CCTV log shows the customer was not in the branch at the time the change was recorded as 'customer present'.
Ms Serrano's own account received cash deposits of about EUR 14,000 over the same period, above her salary pattern.
state.employee_statement: When asked informally by her manager, Ms Serrano said she 'only helped customers who asked for online banking'.
state.access_log_detail: On four of the seven days, Ms Serrano's user ID was active while her badge shows her at a training course in another building; IT confirms the ID was used from her usual branch workstation. Her password was last changed in March, and IT has no record of a reported compromise.
state.branch_practice: Colleagues say branch staff sometimes log in for each other when a workstation is slow, although the IT policy forbids sharing credentials; one colleague said Ms Serrano's password 'was on a sticky note under the keyboard for a while'.
state.customer_contacts: Two of the seven customers, contacted by the investigations unit, said they had never asked for online banking and did not recognise the new phone numbers; the others have not yet been reached.
state.third_receiving_account: The third receiving account is held by a man with no known link to Ms Serrano; its bank reports it was opened in April with a foreign passport and has received payments from several other banks' customers.
state.new_device_data: The new devices used to activate online banking on the seven accounts were two phones; one of them has also logged into Ms Serrano's personal online banking at our bank on several occasions.
state.policy: INT-1 §2: Suspected internal fraud is referred to the Internal Investigations unit and Financial Crime the same day. §3: Do not alert the employee; restrict their system access pending investigation. §4: Affected customers' accounts are secured and customers contacted by the investigations unit.
state.manager_action: The branch manager asked Ms Serrano informally about the changes on 09/12 before the referral.
